description: We are MOTHI MANSA, our skills span remote sensing, data analysis, web development, research and design. We believe finding the solution to a problem the quickest is only part of the critical thinking process, nurturing the patience to admire the elegance of the problem really makes for an neat and exquisite solution. By this motto, we plan to provide with a small yet an effective and intuitive solution to the challenge we decide to face.
summary:
The lack of awarness regarding meterological and agroclimatological data, and goverment provided services such as “Krishi Vigyan Kendra” in India causes negative impact on agricultural sector. This problem created a need to provide farmers across the nation with a suggestion tool that takes into consideration their priorities and constraints to provide them with suitable crop rotations subjected to data from various resources provided by NASA, ISRO & The Government Of India.

Our goal is to translate NASA satellite data into simple, location-specific advice that helps farmers choose and rotate crops as the climate shifts.
details:
What it does and how it works
Field Shift is a web tool that turns NASA satellite data into simple crop decisions for farmers. The user picks a location, such as a field in Ahilyanagar, Maharashtra. The app then pulls 30 m Landsat NDVI and surface temperature, SMAP L4 soil moisture, GPM IMERG rainfall, MODIS land surface temperature, FluxSat GPP and NASA POWER weather data. It scores crops against these conditions and returns a ranked list with a plain-language reason for each. An Interactive Crop Rotation Planner suggests what to grow next, and a KVK crop calendar by district adds local context.

Benefits
Farmers get field-level insight without technical knowledge. Advice comes with emoji verdicts and simple steps, in English, Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, Bengali, Tamil and Telugu. Better crop and water decisions can reduce input costs and the risk of crop failure.

Intended impact
We want to close the gap between freely available NASA data and the people who need it. Our aim is to help farmers in semi-arid regions adapt to erratic rainfall and rising heat, and to give extension workers a data-driven reference.

Tools and technology

  • Python, FastAPI (backend), HTML/CSS/JavaScript and Leaflet (frontend)
  • Google Earth Engine, NASA POWER, NASA Earthdata (via earthaccess, rasterio, rioxarray, geopandas)
  • VS Code and Git for development
  • Claude and Gemini for coding, data workflows and drafting; Canva AI for the team logo; Adobe Firefly for presentation maps and images
  • No special hardware: it runs in a browser, with the backend on a standard computer

Creativity
Field Shift combines several NASA datasets in one view and explains them the way a farmer would, with local languages, reasons for each recommendation, and the district crop calendar alongside the satellite insights.

Factors we considered

  • Language and literacy, so the interface is simple and multilingual
  • Data resolution limits, since different datasets cover different scales
  • Rule-of-thumb crop thresholds that need refining with local agronomic data
  • Local farming practice, through the KVK calendar
  • Accessibility, which is why we plan to deploy the backend online so farmers can use it on a phone
